vignette: A 55-year-old man has sudden weakness of the left leg with a normal arm and face. He is apathetic and answers slowly, and his wife says he has been incontinent since the event. A grasp reflex is present on the left.

options.text: Right middle cerebral artery, superior division

explanation: Leg-predominant weakness with abulia, incontinence and a grasp reflex is the anterior cerebral artery territory: the paracentral lobule (leg), the medial frontal micturition and motivation areas and the cingulate cortex. An MCA lesion would weaken the face and arm.
